metadata.case_name: LEE LAP MAN v. FUNG KING FAI

injuries.description: Loss of sight in left eye / no perception of light
source: The left eve demonstrated no Perception of light.

injuries.description: 1.5 cm laceration of left upper eye-lid
source: a 1.5 cm laceration of his left upper eye-lid
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of eyelid or periocular area

injuries.description: Three small pieces of broken glass entered left eye (foreign bodies)
source: three small pieces of broken glass entered his left eye
injuries.icd_description: Retained foreign body following penetrating wound of orbit

injuries.description: Abrasions to his face; bruises around left eye
source: The plaintiff suffered abrasions to his face, bruises around his left eye

injuries.description: Fracture of the orbital region; fracture of the lesser wing of the sphemoid; fracture of the medial wall of the orbit with entrapment of the medial rectus
injuries.body_part: orbital region / medial wall of the orbit / lesser wing of the sphemoid
source: a CAT scan revealed a fracture of the orbital region, fracture of the lesser wing of the sphemoid and a fracture of the medial wall of the orbit with entrapment of the medial rectus.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

manifestations.description: loss of sight in one eye
loss of three dimensional vision and with it the capacity to swiftly and accurately judge distance and depth
eye feeling tired after working for a long time
the left eye may become divergent (deviate outwards) causing a cosmetically unattractive appearance
works more slowly compared to other employees with the same length of training

treatments_received: admitted to the United Christian Hospital where the three pieces of glass were removed
admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital
surgical toilet and suturing of the forehead laceration
discharged on 14th August 1987 with follow up at the Yaumatei Opthalmic Clinic
treatments_future: corrective surgery for divergent eye (strabismus surgery) - plaintiff will require such corrective surgery at least once in the future

losses.description: the left eye may become divergent (deviate outwards) causing a cosmetically unattractive appearance; such a development could be corrected surgically
The plaintiff would never become a first class hairdresser, and will never be as good a hairdresser as the average hairdresser with both eyes; slower and less able to perform some hairdressing tasks
